### Response body size, timeouts and connection caps

-`Config.MaxResponseBodySize` (default 100 MiB, a negative value for none) bounds upstream response bodies to protect against memory exhaustion. `Config.MaxConnsPerHost` (default `1024`) caps concurrent connections per upstream to limit fan-out from a single hot host. `Balancer` also bounds each request with `Config.Timeout` (default one second).

+`Config.MaxResponseBodySize` (default 100 MiB, a negative value for none) bounds upstream response bodies to protect against memory exhaustion. A body the proxy streams, a response set to stream with `c.Response().StreamBody` or one read by a client that streams, is held to it as well, which fasthttp does not do for a stream: a body that declares more is refused before any of it is sent, and one that passes the bound without declaring its length ends the response early. A `ModifyResponse` hook that reads a streamed body into memory takes in no more than the bound: the read fails past it. A `Config.Client` keeps the bounds of its own clients: the default does not apply to it, only a size you set, and only to a body it streams. `Config.MaxConnsPerHost` (default `1024`) caps concurrent connections per upstream to limit fan-out from a single hot host. `Balancer` also bounds each request with `Config.Timeout` (default one second).

`proxy.Balancer` takes its `proxy.Config` as an optional variadic argument, like the other middleware constructors. `Servers` (or a custom `Client` with `Clients`) is required, so `proxy.Balancer()` without a config panics at startup, as `proxy.Balancer(proxy.Config{})` does, and so does a `Client` without `Clients`. A server without a port is dialed on the port of its scheme, and each server is reached with its own scheme, so an `https` upstream works behind a plain-HTTP listener.

-The proxy is secure by default. Upstreams that resolve to loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, CGNAT or other special-use addresses (IPv6 transition forms included) are refused, and so are schemes other than `http` and `https` and HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects. Every request is bounded: `Balancer` buffers at most `MaxResponseBodySize` of an upstream response, 100 MiB unless set (a negative value lifts the bound; a `Config.Client` keeps the bounds of its own clients), and the client behind `Do`, `DoRedirects`, `Forward`, `DomainForward` and `BalancerForward` gives each request, and each redirect hop, 30 seconds for the whole exchange, connect and body included, unless `DoTimeout` or `DoDeadline` set the request's own bound, and buffers at most 100 MiB of a response, until `proxy.WithClient` replaces it. Hop-by-hop headers are stripped, and `Balancer`, `Forward`, `DomainForward` and `BalancerForward` overwrite `X-Real-IP` with `c.IP()`; with `Do`, `DoTimeout`, `DoDeadline` and `DoRedirects` you set it yourself. The trailer section of a chunked request is dropped instead of reaching the upstream as header lines, the trailer section of an upstream's chunked response is dropped instead of reaching the client as header lines, whether the client buffers the response or streams it, and a forwarding header sent on several lines keeps them in the order they were received; a request carrying more than 64 forwarding lines, the `X-Real-IP` line the proxy writes included, is refused with `431 Request Header Fields Too Large`. To proxy to an internal host, relax the policy with `proxy.WithSecurityPolicy` (or `Config.SecurityPolicy` for `Balancer`), for example `proxy.SecurityPolicy{AllowPrivateIPs: true}`, before you build `DomainForward` or `BalancerForward`: they check their upstreams when the handler is built and panic on a rejected one. Keep the policy installed while they serve: `Forward`, `DomainForward` and `BalancerForward` read it on every request, whereas `Balancer` reads it once, when it is built. See [Security](./middleware/proxy.md#security).

`ErrUpstreamHostUnresolvable` is new: a name that cannot be resolved, or that resolves to no address, is rejected with an error that matches it and `ErrUpstreamHostBlocked` both, and `errors.As` finds the `*net.DNSError` of the lookup. A host with only IPv6 addresses and `DialDualStack` off fails with an error that matches neither, where it matched `ErrUpstreamHostBlocked` before. An address `net/url` cannot parse is rejected with `ErrUpstreamHostInvalid` and the `*url.Error` wrapped beside it, so the message of that error carries the parse error. The time `DoTimeout`, `DoDeadline` or `Config.Timeout` allows bounds the lookup and the connects of the request as well; a connect that nothing bounds has five seconds, as before.
